ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, beneficial owners, and senior persons against the New Zealand Sanctions List, the United Nations Consolidated Consolidated List, the Office of European Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit's list of persons of interest. Additionally, conduct enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined by the AML/CFT Act, including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and international organization PEPs. Screening must be conducted at the time of onboarding, on an ongoing basis, and upon any change in ownership or control. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Company Name Reservation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or Māori, with phonetic transliteration permitted. The name must be identical or similar to an existing name, and must not be misleading. The name must include the legal element 'Limited' or 'Ltd' for a limited company. The system applies a four-tier naming convention: exact match, similar match, phonetic match, and visual match. Any name likely to be confused with an existing name will be rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name reservation is rejected, the applicant may apply for a review by the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days of the rejection notice. The review must be submitted in writing, stating the reason for appeal and providing evidence that the name is not misleading or prohibited. The applicant will receive a decision within 15 working days. If the review is unsuccessful, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under section 21 of the Companies Act 1993. The appeal must be filed within 20 working days of the Registrar's decision. The applicant may also propose an alternative name for immediate consideration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox addresses are generally not permissible for a multi-family office (MFO) in New Zealand. The AML/CFT Act requires reporting institutions to have a registered presence and to maintain records at a physical address. The Inland Revenue Department and the Companies Office require a physical registered office address that is not a PO Box or virtual office. Banks and financial institutions will reject a virtual office address for account opening and will require a physical business address for due diligence purposes. Therefore, a physical office in New Zealand is mandatory for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High risk of unannounced physical inspections by the Companies Office, the Inland Revenue Department, and the Financial Police. The risk is quantified as 80% within the first year of incorporation for high-risk AML entities such as MFOs. Checklist items: (1) Registered office must be a physical address in New Zealand, not a PO Box; (2) The office must have a visible sign with the company name; (3) The office must be accessible during business hours; (4) The company must maintain physical records of AML/CFT compliance, UBO information, and financial statements; (5) The office must have a dedicated phone line and email address; (6) The office must be able to produce original documents upon request.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), in particular sections 12-23 (incorporation, constitution and certificate of incorporation), sections 24-36 (share capital and issue of shares), sections 151-153 (appointment of directors), section 189 (registered office), sections 191-201 (address for service and registers), and section 362 (rights of appeal). The Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 govern the licensing of the multi-family office operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating through the New Zealand Companies Register online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online Incorporation Application via the New Zealand Companies Register (the electronic equivalent of the statutory incorporation application and Form 2 shareholders and directors consents), together with the proposed constitution, consent to appointment of directors, consent to shareholding, and registered office details.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no statutory minimum paid-up share capital, no minimum issued share value, and no escrow or blocked capital account requirement. The company must have at least one shareholder and one issued share, and each first director must certify that the company will be able to pay its debts as they become due in the ordinary course of business. Separately, an FMA-licensed Discretionary Investment Management Service provider must demonstrate adequate financial resources and operational capacity to the satisfaction of the Financial Markets Authority.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF NZ_LTD (the Company), DULY CONVENED AND HELD ON [DATE] AT [INSERT REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS], NEW ZEALAND. ATTENDEES AND QUORUM: The following directors of the Company were present in person or by electronic attendance: [Insert names of each director]. The chairman confirmed that the meeting was duly constituted and that a quorum was present under the Company constitution and the Companies Act 1993. RESOLVED THAT the registration of the Company under the Companies Act 1993, including the filing of the online incorporation application, the constitution, the consent forms of the directors and shareholders, and the registered office details with the New Zealand Companies Office, be and is hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved in all respects. RESOLVED THAT the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed and adopted at [Insert full physical street address, not a post office box], New Zealand, and that this address be filed with the Registrar of Companies as the Company's registered office in accordance with section 189 of the Companies Act 1993. RESOLVED THAT the share capital of the Company be and is hereby subscribed, issued, and allotted as follows on the date of incorporation: [Shareholder A] subscribes for [Number] ordinary shares at NZ$[Amount] per share; [Shareholder B] subscribes for [Number] ordinary shares at NZ$[Amount] per share; and any additional subscribers set out in the share register subscribe as approved. The board accepts the subscriptions, directs the allotment of the shares, and confirms that the consideration received, recorded, and credited to issued share capital shall be fully paid and non-assessable shares. RESOLVED THAT [Insert director A] be and is hereby appointed as a director of the Company, [Insert director B] be and is hereby appointed as a director of the Company, and [Insert name] be and is hereby appointed as chairperson of the Board, each to hold office until removal by resolution or as otherwise provided by the Companies Act 1993. RESOLVED THAT the banking mandate of the Company be and is hereby established, and the board authorizes the opening, operation, and closure of corporate bank accounts, custody accounts, and electronic banking facilities with any bank, custodian, or financial institution selected by the officers, including but not limited to institutions supporting SWIFT interbank and custody wire payment rails. RESOLVED THAT any two directors are authorized, as designated signatories, to sign all account opening documents, mandates, SWIFT instructions, letters, agreements, and indemnities on behalf of the Company, provided that all transactions comply with the Company's anti-money laundering and countering financing of terrorism obligations, financial crime screening policies, and internal approvals matrix. RESOLVED THAT the board approves the appointment of [Insert compliance officer], [Insert risk officer], and [Insert company secretary], with authority to implement the corporate governance manual, maintain the statutory registers, file annual returns, liaise with the Companies Office and Inland Revenue, and execute all administrative documents incidental to the Company's formation and ongoing governance. RESOLVED THAT the authorised officers and directors be and are hereby directed to proceed with Inland Revenue tax registration, New Zealand Business Number registration, registration on the Financial Service Providers Register, application for the appropriate licence under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, and any other regulatory filing necessary for the lawful operation of the multi-family office, and to pay all relevant fees from company funds. RESOLVED THAT the minutes of this meeting, once signed by the chairperson, be recorded in the Company's minute book and be conclusive evidence of these resolutions. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT all actions taken by the directors and officers in connection with the matters contemplated by these resolutions be and are hereby ratified, confirmed, and adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Availability Clearance, and Structure Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, New Zealand Companies Register online portal (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name availability search on the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm that the proposed company name, NZ_LTD, is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company name or reserved name. Confirm that the name does not include prohibited terms, does not imply an affiliation with the Crown, and satisfies the name rules under the Companies Act 1993. Prepare and approve the constitutional documents, including the company constitution, directors' consents, shareholders' consents, share allocation schedule, and designated registered office address. If a preferred name is available but is to be held before incorporation, file a name reservation application and pay the reservation fee. Confirm the exact legal entity form, share class designations, voting rights, and restrictions appropriate for a multi-family office serving multiple private client families.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and alternative names
Name search results or name reservation reference
Draft constitution of the company
Share allocation and shareholders' proposed registered details
Proposed registered office physical address in New Zealand
Directors' consent forms and identity verification documents
Initial board resolution approving the name and structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search reveals an identical or confusingly similar name, select the next available alternative and file a new name reservation. If the Registrar issues a name direction or requests additional explanation, respond in writing through the Companies Register portal within 20 working days, provide evidence of legitimate use, request the removal of any misleading name, or appeal the decision to the High Court under section 362 of the Companies Act 1993 as applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing and Certificate Issue
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online incorporation application through the New Zealand Companies Register. Provide the company name, constitution adoption election or default statutory rules, registered office physical address, address for service, directors' full details and consents, shareholders' full details, share allocation, and the statement confirming each director consents to act and is eligible under the Companies Act 1993. Upload or attach the executed constitution and all mandatory consent forms. Authorize the applicant or agent to submit the application, review the pre-filing summary, and make payment of the prescribed filing fee. The Registrar will issue a Certificate of Incorporation electronically upon verification. The company comes into existence on the date and time stated in the certificate. After incorporation, retain the certificate in the company's statutory records, create the share register, and file any required notice within the statutory timeline.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation (issued after filing)
Online incorporation application submission summary
Executed constitution
Consent to act as director (Form for each director)
Consent to act as shareholder and share subscription forms
Registered office address and address for service declaration
Applicant or agent authorisation form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office raises a query or suspends the application, respond to the notice through the online portal within the time requested, usually 20 working days, by providing corrected information or the missing consent forms. If the application is rejected, remedy the specified defect, resubmit the application with the revised details, and pay any new filing fee if applicable. If the Registrar refuses to issue a certificate, request a written statement of reasons, apply for internal reconsideration, and where necessary appeal to the High Court under section 362 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, IRD Number, and New Zealand Business Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue, New Zealand (IRD), and New Zealand Business Number Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Certificate of Incorporation is issued, apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number for the company using the appropriate company tax registration form or through the myIR business portal. Provide the Certificate of Incorporation, company constitution, director and shareholder details, business address, principal business activity code (ISIC 6430 / portfolio advisory), and expected date of commencement of financial services. Register for GST if the company expects taxable supplies to exceed NZD 60,000 per twelve-month period or if registration is otherwise required or desirable. Apply for a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) through the NZBN Registry; the NZBN is issued automatically for new companies but must be verified and linked with tax and company records. The company should also confirm its provisional tax and PAYE obligations if it will employ staff. Instruct the company accountants to align the tax registration record with the multi-family office fee structure and cross-border custody arrangements.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
Company constitution
Directors' and shareholders' details and birth dates
Company application for IRD number (company registration form)
Registered office and physical business address details
Principal business activity and projected revenue statement
GST registration application, if applicable
Appointment of tax agent and accountant authority letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue queries the application or requests further information, respond through the myIR portal or by written submission within the stated deadline, supply the requested identification documents or director details, and correct any typographical mismatch between the Companies Office record and IRD record. If the IRD number is not issued within the expected timeframe, contact the IRD business contact centre and escalate through the agent channel. If the NZBN is not activated automatically, request activation through the NZBN support desk with the certificate of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) Registration and Anti-Money Laundering / Countering Financing of Terrorism Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Service Providers Register, administered by the New Zealand Companies Office / Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, with AML/CFT supervision by the Financial Markets Authority as the MFO's principal supervisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company on the Financial Service Providers Register under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008. Identify the precise financial services to be supplied, including discretionary investment management services, portfolio administration, custody-related services, and financial advice. Nominate a financial dispute resolution scheme and enrol the company as a member. Prepare a documented AML/CFT business risk assessment and an AML/CFT compliance programme addressing customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence for high-risk private client families, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, suspicious activity reporting, record keeping, and employee training. Appoint the AML/CFT compliance officer and audit the adequacy of governance arrangements. The FMA will expect board-level ownership of the risk assessment and programme. If the service activity crosses into managed investment schemes, identify whether separate registration or licensing is required.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
FSPR registration application and FSP service list
Business risk assessment and AML/CFT compliance programme
AML/CFT compliance officer appointment letter
Membership certificate from approved dispute resolution scheme
Directors' attestations and personal due diligence forms
Organisation chart and governance policies
Charges and fees schedule for advisory services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSPR application is queried or suspended, submit corrected information and the missing AML/CFT documentation through the online portal. If the chosen dispute resolution scheme declines membership, select another approved scheme and update the register. If the AML/CFT supervisor issues an inspection report or remedial direction, prepare a corrective action plan within the required timeframe, appoint external compliance advisers where needed, and if a decision is adverse, exercise any right of reconsideration or apply to the High Court for judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 DIMS Licensing and Final Governance Implementation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA), New Zealand, together with the New Zealand Companies Office for final statutory register updates
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit a complete licensing application to the Financial Markets Authority for a Discretionary Investment Management Service (DIMS) licence under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, because the multi-family office will exercise discretion in managing client portfolios. The application must describe the investment architecture, asset classes, custody arrangements, delegation framework, conflict of interest management, valuation policies, risk management, compliance systems, governance, and responsible persons. Demonstrate that the company has adequate financial resources, professional indemnity insurance arrangements, fit and proper directors, and robust business continuity plans. Include the AML/CFT programme submitted in step four, the FSPR registration confirmation, and the dispute resolution scheme membership. The FMA will conduct a gateway assessment and may request detailed responses. After licence grant, execute the corporate governance manual, board charters, client agreements, global investment policy statements, and annual compliance plan. Update the shareholders register and annual return and upload the licence details to the Companies Office if required.
required_dossiers: FMA DIMS licence application form and supplemental schedules
AML/CFT business risk assessment and programme
FSPR registration and dispute resolution scheme evidence
Business plan, operational budget, and financial resources statement
Professional indemnity insurance policy certificate and broker letter
Fit and proper evidence for directors and responsible persons
Client custody and SWIFT wire protocol and delegation agreements
Compliance manual, conflict of interest register, and complaints process
Board resolutions approving the final governance architecture
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FMA requests further information under its statutory powers, respond by the deadline and supply complete responses to all gateway criteria. If the application is recommended for decline, provide submissions and may request an opportunity to appear before the FMA or its delegate. If the licence is declined, revise the application with strengthened governance and capital arrangements, reapply, or apply to the High Court for review of the decision if grounds exist. Throughout the process, maintain communication with the FMA relationship manager and promptly remedy any compliance deficiencies identified.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for industrial or physical licensing because the scope is a multi-family office providing discretionary portfolio advisory services under ISIC 6430 / NAICS 523920 and does not operate a manufacturing, assembly, chemical, warehousing, or extractive facility. The applicable regulatory authority for the financial services licence is the Financial Markets Authority, and the Financial Service Providers Register is administered by the New Zealand Companies Office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable as a physical or industrial operating permit. The statutory financial service authorisation comprises: (1) registration on the Financial Service Providers Register under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; and (2) a Discretionary Investment Management Service (DIMS) licence under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 for the portfolio management services to be supplied to multiple private client families.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no Environmental Impact Assessment is triggered because the company will not construct or operate a physical industrial plant, chemical process, manufacturing line, solid waste facility, or storage warehouse.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - the business is classified purely as a financial and consulting service with no physical footprint beyond a standard office tenancy.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the company has no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, hazardous waste generation, stationary combustion sources, or physical pollutant load requiring consenting under the Resource Management Act 1991.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for civil defense fire permits and industrial structural load certification because no industrial premises or hazardous goods storage will be operated. The company must nevertheless comply with general workplace law, maintain a safe office under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, hold a current building warrant of fitness for any leased premises under the Building Act 2004, and observe Fire and Emergency New Zealand egress, alarm, and evacuation requirements for its professional office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand (Inland Revenue, IRD); online electronic portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz/myir). Company registration is administered by the New Zealand Companies Office (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A New Zealand incorporated limited company is formed under the Companies Act 1993 via the New Zealand Companies Office. On incorporation, the Companies Office electronically transmits the company particulars to Inland Revenue, which automatically allocates a New Zealand IRD number, the statutory tax identification number for income tax, GST, employer obligations and other tax purposes. The IRD number is made available to the company through the Companies Office registry and myIR. A non-resident company not incorporated in New Zealand but carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand must separately apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number through the non-resident company registration process in myIR and must provide certified certificate of incorporation from its home jurisdiction, constitutional documents and ultimate beneficial ownership details. The IRD number is required before any GST registration can be activated and must be quoted on all tax returns and correspondence with Inland Revenue.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available. A closely held eligible New Zealand company may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) treatment under Subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, causing income and expenses to be attributed to shareholders; however, the LTC election is generally unavailable to a multi-family office owned by corporate trustees or with more than five shareholders and is therefore not assumed. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 apply and are not elective; there is no hybrid mismatch check-the-box election in New Zealand.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, administered by Inland Revenue; a national VAT-type tax with no subnational sales or use tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies (excluding GST) supplied in New Zealand in any 12-month period under section 51 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Exempt financial supplies, including many discretionary portfolio management services supplied by a multi-family office, are not taxable supplies counted toward the threshold, although voluntary registration is available. Non-resident suppliers of remote services into New Zealand must register for GST when their New Zealand remote-services turnover exceeds NZD 60,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, pre-clearance, API stamping or anti-fraud digital stamping regime exists in New Zealand. GST invoices are required for taxable supplies of NZD 50 or more and must contain the prescribed particulars in section 24 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Electronic invoicing is voluntary and operates under the New Zealand National E-Invoicing Framework using the Peppol network; GST returns are filed electronically through myIR. Records must be retained for at least 7 years and made available to Inland Revenue on request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, exports of goods may be zero-rated where ownership in the goods is transferred before or at the time of removal from New Zealand and the supplier retains evidence that the goods were exported from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply. Services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of performance are zero-rated where the services are not supplied directly in connection with land or movable property in New Zealand and are not otherwise treated as supplied in New Zealand. For a multi-family office, the supply of discretionary portfolio advisory services to a non-resident client must first be classified: if the services constitute GST-exempt financial services under section 3 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, no GST is charged and there is no zero-rating claim; if the services are taxable, the export service criteria in section 11 must be evidenced by the client's non-resident status, the performance out of New Zealand or receipt outside New Zealand, and absence of any direct connection to New Zealand property. Refunds of input tax attributable to exported taxable supplies are claimed through the normal GST return; overpayments are refundable by Inland Revenue, but the zero-rating evidence remains subject to audit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service Export Entry (electronic declaration filed through the Trade Single Window)
Bill of Lading, Sea Waybill or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from New Zealand
Commercial invoice, packing list and export-related carriage documents
Bank foreign exchange credit advice or inward remittance advice showing the export goods or services proceeds credited to the New Zealand company's bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may scrutinise export zero-rating claims during GST audits and refund reviews. If the supplier cannot substantiate the export within 28 days for goods or cannot prove the non-resident, offshore supply criteria for services, the supply is recharacterised as taxable at 15% and the resulting GST shortfall is assessed with use-of-money interest and late payment penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994. Deliberate or fraudulent misstatements attract shortfall penalties under sections 141A to 141D of the Tax Administration Act 1994, including up to 150% of the tax shortfall in the case of evasion and 100% for an unacceptable tax position taken without reasonable care, and may give rise to criminal liability. Record-keeping for the substantiation documents is mandatory for at least 7 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains an open, freely convertible current and capital account regime. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand is responsible for currency issuance and prudential regulation but does not impose exchange controls, licensing for inward/outward remittances, or mandatory conversion of export proceeds. Both residents and non-residents may transact in NZD and foreign currencies through authorised banks. The Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 and Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 focus on conduct and verification rather than quantitative foreign exchange restrictions. Capital injections and profit repatriation require appropriate underlying documentation, including shareholder resolutions, trust distributions, audited financial statements, and standard bank customer due diligence. There are no surrender requirements nor forced conversion ratios. Certain real-property and significant-business acquisition transactions by overseas persons may require screening under the Overseas Investment Act 2005, but that is not a foreign exchange restriction. Dividend, interest, service fee, and liquidation distributions can generally be remitted at bank buying and selling rates; banking counterparties may require a tax confirmation such as a New Zealand IRD certificate or certificate of residence. Overall, New Zealand is a high-convertibility, low-friction jurisdiction for treasury operations, with market-based pricing and deep NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, and NZD/CNH liquidity through the domestic interbank market. The key practical friction is not foreign exchange control but KYC/AML evidence and business substance verification for a high-risk multi-family office.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement exists under New Zealand law. Exporters may retain foreign currency receipts in approved overseas accounts or convert freely. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand does not prescribe timelines or conversion ratios. Reporting obligations are limited to AML/CFT transaction records, tax declarations, and OECD country-by-country reporting where applicable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Business Transaction and Foreign Currency Account
Corporate Everyday Account and ASB Foreign Currency Account
Business Account and Global Markets Foreign Currency Account
Corporate Cash Management Account and Multi-Currency Account
Business Account with Foreign Currency Capabilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI cross-border viability is legally constrained. New Zealand does not have a dedicated EMI licensing framework for standalone e-money institutions; non-bank payment service providers must register on the Financial Service Providers Register and comply with the AML/CFT Act, but they cannot take deposits or participate directly in the Exchange Settlement Account System. Such providers typically act as payment facilitators and require a sponsor bank for settlement. For a licensed multi-family office requiring custody-grade cash management, segregated client funds, and high-value cross-border wires, pure fintech EMIs rank Low in viability. A reputable Tier-1 bank is required for capital subscriptions, fiduciary holdings, and trust disbursements. Fintechs can supplement expense payments and FX comparison but cannot replace domestic clearing rails or provide legal banking credit and custody services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand banks accept a mix of in-branch and remote verification. Under the AML/CFT Act, identity must be verified before the relationship is established; face-to-face verification in a New Zealand branch is the strongest option, but banks may permit remote verification using New Zealand notary, Law Society certification, JCAP certification, or a consular officer of a recognised jurisdiction. For a multi-family office classified as High_Risk_Special_License, regulatory and bank policy expectations generally require statutory directors, signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners to complete a physical or video-conference identity review with bank compliance, plus an independent credit and trust-structure opinion. In practice, at least one director and one beneficial owner must meet with the bank relationship and compliance team before discretionary mandates are operationalised. Purely remote, proxy- or nominee-only opening is rarely accepted without a referral from a reputable correspondent bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dispersed beneficial ownership through multiple New Zealand and offshore discretionary trusts where no single natural person owns more than 25%
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trust deeds and registered variations; trust settlement deeds; tax residence certificates for each trustee; a formal beneficial-ownership spreadsheet mapping every protector, settlor, and beneficiary class; a legal opinion from a New Zealand law firm under the AML/CFT Beneficial Ownership Guidance; and independent verification of the source of trust incubation funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated family office receives fund contributions from high-risk jurisdictions, cryptocurrency liquidation, or opaque private company dividends
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For each funding source, provide bank statements and transaction narratives from the originator banks; incorporation and tax records of underlying companies; audited financial statements; IRD or tax compliance certificates; traceability reports for digital assets; and an independent source-of-wealth report prepared by a certified accountant or forensic firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discretionary portfolio management over multiple client families creates an omnibus account risk and a horizontal naming mismatch between the entity and underlying family principals
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Individual client onboarding files for each family; signed Investment Management Agreements; disclosed fee schedules and performance terms; risk profile questionnaires; client-specific standing investment instructions; sanctions and PEP screening screenshots; annual AML compliance attestation; and confirmation that client money is held under securities and custody rules with separate client money reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected or high-frequency cross-border inflows from jurisdictions with weak beneficial ownership registries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A board resolution authorising the treasury mandate; current and 24-month cash-flow forecasts; copies of original SWIFT MT103 instructions with purpose code; counterparty KYC on remitting institutions; letters from foreign banks confirming the beneficial ownership of the remitter; and tax disclosures and source-of-funds declarations certified by an accountant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For equity capital injection into the NZ Ltd, route SWIFT MT103 from the ultimate parent or beneficial owner's bank to the company's designated NZD account at a New Zealand Tier-1 bank. Use Field 50K to show the actual beneficial remitter, Field 59 for the NZ Ltd beneficiary with the account number, and Field 70 with the exact purpose: SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION - NZD or DIRECTOR'S LOAN - NZD. New Zealand does not require resident banks to obtain Reserve Bank approval for inward remittances, but the receiving bank will perform sanctions and source-of-funds screening and may request a shareholder resolution allotting shares, a statutory declaration, and a board resolution confirming the capital injection. After receipt, prepare a capital contribution verification file that includes the bank confirmation, FX dealing ticket if any currency conversion occurred, board minute, and the share allocation filing on the New Zealand Companies Register. If the equity owner is an overseas person acquiring sensitive land or media assets, the Overseas Investment Act screening must be assessed before completion; otherwise no foreign exchange consent is required. Ongoing subscriptions from family trusts should include the trust deed and full beneficial ownership confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for straightforward payables such as management fees, distributions, trust payments, and discretionary investment disbursements. For documentary trade settlements, use Commercial Letters of Credit via MT700 or MT707 where the NZ corporate is importer or exporter; banks issue letters of credit providing payment against compliant shipping documents. For lower-value or better-controlled flows, Documentary Collections using MT400 for a bill of exchange or MT420 for other document collections mitigate bank credit risk while preserving document control. Multi-family office investment disbursements should be executed through the institutional custody wire desk with the instruction coded as CUSTODY_WIRE, and any underlying FX should be executed through the bank global markets desk with clear debit of the NZD and credit of the target currency.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts on deliverable NZD pairs including NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/CNH, NZD/JPY, and NZD/AUD for trade-related and balance-sheet hedging
Non-deliverable forwards on restricted or less-liquid emerging market currencies, subject to bank credit approval and the existence of an underlying exposure

Cross-currency swaps and FX swaps for short-term funding liquidity and balance-sheet hedging under an ISDA Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex, limited to genuine market risk coverage and not speculative trading

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the annual return date, being the anniversary of incorporation; first annual return due one month after the first incorporation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the company and directors to late filing penalties and civil penalties up to NZD 10,000 under the Companies Act 1993. Persistent non-filing across successive years enables the Registrar to initiate administrative strike-off and removal from the Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Statutory Audit Package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; New Zealand Companies Office and Financial Markets Authority (FMA) where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 March balance date, audited annual financial statements and annual report to shareholders must be completed and filed by 30 September (within 6 months after balance date).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with financial reporting obligations under the Companies Act 1993 and Financial Reporting Act 2013 is a director offence, with fines up to NZD 20,000, daily penalties, and Companies Register removal proceedings for large companies failing to file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 tax return and terminal tax payment are due by 7 July following the tax year; tax agent extension may defer filing to 31 March of the next year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and late payment penalties apply under the Tax Administration Act 1994: initial late payment penalty, incremental monthly penalties, and use-of-money interest on outstanding tax; prosecution and further penalties may follow repeated non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Under the elected taxable period (monthly, bi-monthly, or six-monthly), each GST return and payment is due on the 28th day after the end of the taxable period; the annual cycle produces 12, 6, or 2 statutory filing events respectively.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file GST returns or pay GST attracts the IRD late filing penalty schedule, incremental monthly penalties, and use-of-money interest; deliberate evasion may lead to investigation and criminal sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT Annual Compliance and Independent Assurance Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) as AML/CFT supervisor for licensed financial advice providers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the financial year end, or as directed in the FMA AML/CFT supervisory programme, including annual independent assurance testing of the AML/CFT programme and risk assessment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Breaches of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 expose the reporting entity to civil penalties up to NZD 2 million per contravention, compliance orders, and AML/CFT licence revocation or suspension.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) as administrator of the Financial Service Providers Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due each year by 30 June; all financial service providers must complete the online annual confirmation and pay the renewal fee before the 1 July start of the next registration period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm and pay by 30 June results in removal from the FSPR; operating without registration is an offence under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, with fines up to NZD 300,000 for a body corporate.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified audit is mandatory under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Companies Act 1993 where, for two consecutive annual accounting periods, the company exceeds any of the following thresholds: (a) total balance-sheet assets above NZD 30 million (approx. USD 18.5 million); (b) total annual revenue above NZD 60 million (approx. USD 37 million); (c) 50 or more full-time equivalent employees; or (d) the company is an FMC reporting entity/issuer, or is otherwise classified as a large entity. In all cases, FMA licence conditions for an ISIC 6430 multi-family office may independently require an audit or assurance engagement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand equivalents of IFRS (NZ IFRS); reduced disclosure concession via NZ IFRS RDR for eligible small and medium companies; statutory framework per Financial Reporting Act 2013, Companies Act 1993, External Reporting Board standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no standalone UBO return; however, the Companies Office annual return captures current director, shareholder, and significant shareholding information. Any transfer of shares must be recorded in the Register of Members and notified to the Companies Office within 30 days of the share register update. Under AML/CFT law, the licensed multi-family office must perform annual enhanced due diligence on ultimate beneficial owners, maintain an internal UBO/control register, and report material beneficial-ownership changes to the FMA within the prescribed notification window.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday exists for Multi-Family Office services in New Zealand. The effective cash tax rate is reduced by full deductibility of arm's length operating costs (e.g., custodian fees, legal advice, software, occupancy). The R&D Tax Incentive (15% credit) is unavailable to portfolio advisory activities. Imputation credits attach to dividends, eliminating double taxation at shareholder level. Foreign Investment Fund (FIF) rules may deem offshore portfolio returns as taxable income. No preferential regime applies to MFO operations.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory expiry under s IA 3 Income Tax Act 2007; subject to 49% shareholder continuity or the business continuity test in s IA 5)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Income Tax Return for Companies) filed solely through the Inland Revenue 'myIR' secure online portal. Electronic filing is mandatory for medium and large taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return with three mandatory provisional tax instalments during the year (payment frequency, not filing frequency).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date: IR4 due 7 July (electronic) / 7 June (paper). For a non-standard balance date: due on the 7th day of the 4th month following the balance date (e.g., 30 June balance date due 7 November). Provisional tax instalments for a 31 March balance date fall due 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross income from all business and investment sources, including portfolio management fees, interest, dividends, and realised gains on disposals.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate MFO with a New Zealand fixed establishment must include only New Zealand-source income attributable to that establishment. Offshore fees from non-resident clients are excluded unless the services are rendered through the NZ PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Separate disclosure of interest from New Zealand and overseas sources, and dividends from New Zealand resident companies (gross of imputation credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies should list only interest/dividends with a New Zealand source; foreign passive income should be separately declared to claim treaty or FIF exemptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: salaries, custodian charges, administration, rent, professional fees, and other arm's length outgoings wholly incurred in earning assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be allocated to the New Zealand PE on a fair and consistent basis; head office overheads are deductible only to the extent supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back entertainment costs (50%), fines, capital expenditure, unsubstantiated expenses, and expenditure of a private or capital nature.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident MFOs must adjust any intercompany recharge not at arm's length; disallowed transfer pricing adjustments must be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss after applying tax adjustments (Box1 - Box3 + Box4).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident filers, this box isolates the New Zealand PE result only; worldwide income is ignored for NZ tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible tax losses brought forward from prior years, subject to shareholder continuity (49% minimum) or business continuity test.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses from a non-resident's NZ PE may be carried forward only if the PE maintains the same foreign ownership continuity; a continuity breach invalidates the loss.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deduction of carried-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be a positive number; if losses exceed income, enter zero and carry the loss balance forward.
Non-resident companies use the same 28% rate; no additional branch tax is levied if the PE's after-tax profits are not remitted as dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resident withholding tax (RWT) on interest/dividends, foreign tax credits, imputation credits, and tax paid in a foreign jurisdiction under a DTA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies may claim foreign tax credits only if the underlying income is also taxed in NZ and the credit is permitted under a DTA; RWT credits are available for NZ-source passive income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: If Box 8 exceeds Box 9, residual tax payable; if Box 9 exceeds Box 8, refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any residual tax is payable by the 7th of the filing month; a refund is issued to a foreign bank account but may be subject to a non-resident withholding tax if a dividend is deemed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 for failure to file IR4 by the due date (for medium/large taxpayers; NZ$50 for small). An automatic late payment penalty of 1% per month accrues on any unpaid residual tax. Use-of-money interest (UOMI) is charged daily at the underpayment rate (currently 8.32% p.a. as of April 2025). Directors may be personally liable under s 139 Tax Administration Act 1994 for the company's unpaid PAYE, GST, and certain other taxes.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% NRWT on non-resident dividends paid by a New Zealand resident company; 15% on fully imputed dividends (where imputation credits are attached at the 28% company rate). Treaty rates may reduce the rate further (e.g., 15% under most comprehensive DTAs, 0% for qualifying government or pension entities under certain treaties).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief: (1) The non-resident shareholder must obtain an IRC35 Certificate of Tax Residence from its home tax authority. (2) A certified copy must be lodged with the New Zealand paying company before the dividend payment date. (3) The paying company applies the reduced NRWT rate under the applicable DTA. (4) If excessive withholding occurs, the non-resident may file an IR3NR or IR4 return claiming a refund, or apply to Inland Revenue for a tax credit outcome. (5) The IRC35 must be renewed every three years or upon material change. (6) For interest, foreign lenders may alternatively elect the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) at 2% by the NZ payer in lieu of NRWT, but AIL does not apply to associated-party lenders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 15% NRWT; reduced to 2% AIL where the issuer is approved and the lender is unrelated to the borrower. Royalties: 15% NRWT; treaty rates are generally 10% (most DTAs) or 5% under certain treaties (e.g., NZ-US DTA for industrial/commercial royalties). Management and advisory fees are not subject to NRWT unless the non-resident has a PE in NZ.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10,000,000 aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions in an income year triggers mandatory preparation of both Master File and Local File (New Zealand TP rules effective 1 July 2022). A Country-by-Country Report is required where the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds NZD 1,150,000,000. Documentation must be prepared by the IR4 filing deadline and provided to Inland Revenue within 30 days of request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a dedicated Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code. Instead, the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under s BG 1 Income Tax Act 2007, the business continuity test for loss carryforwards, and the 'central management and control' residence test require an MFO Ltd to possess genuine commercial substance in New Zealand. A land-owning shell company with no directors, employees, or meetings in NZ risks being treated as non-resident (exposing its foreign income to NZ tax) or having its cross-border transactions recharacterised at fair market value. Inland Revenue applies OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and may impose shortfall penalties of 100% of the recharacterised tax adjustment (150% for abusive positions) if transactions lack commercial rationality.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of offshore portfolio income, falsification of management fee records, destruction of transaction ledgers, or preparation of dual sets of financial statements to conceal taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under s 143A and s 143B Tax Administration Act 1994: civil shortfall penalty up to 150% of the evaded tax. Criminal prosecution: imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to NZ$50,000 per offence (s 108 Crimes Act 1961 for forgery if applicable).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the company's tax debts arising from evasion under s 139 and s 140 Tax Administration Act 1994; reckless or fraudulent decisions can trigger director penalty notices, disqualification under the Companies Act 1993, and criminal liability for aiding or abetting tax evasion (s 143 D and 148).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a nominee MFO with no physical office, no substantive employee contracts, and board meetings held entirely offshore, while claiming New Zealand residence and treaty benefits on foreign dividend and interest income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue will recharacterise the arrangement under the GAAR (s BG 1); the tax shortfall is assessed at 28% on all worldwide income if the company is held non-resident, plus a shortfall penalty of 100% (150% for abusive tax position). Groundless DTA claims attract criminal fines under s 143A.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign declarations of residence or treaty eligibility without factual substance face personal liability for penalty tax and interest; they may be prosecuted for 'taking an abusive tax position' under s 141D, leading to imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence on high-risk beneficial owners, failure to report suspicious foreign wire transfers, or processing of wealth management transactions for politically exposed persons without enhanced monitoring, in breach of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties up to NZ$2,000,000 per offence for corporate entities; non-compliance with an audit or enforcement order attracts criminal fines up to NZ$10,000,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years for responsible officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior managers and directors are criminally liable for 'wilful blindness' to money laundering red flags; they face personal fines up to NZ$300,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years under s 90 of the AML/CFT Act. They can also be sued for civil compensation by affected clients.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to a non-resident shareholder trust without withholding NRWT, or falsely classifying dividends as management fees to avoid withholding, or failing to obtain a valid IRC35 before applying treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company is assessed for unreported NRWT plus use-of-money interest. A shortfall penalty of 100% of the NRWT not withheld (150% for intentional evasion) applies. Directors who knowingly caused the non-payment are personally liable for the full NRWT amount under the director penalty regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be issued a personal notice to pay unpaid NRWT; failure to rectify within 30 days makes them personally liable for the entire withheld amount, and further prosecution under s 143 may result in imprisonment up to 5 years.
